summary.headline: ArisInfra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 291 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 31 crore, margin 10.49%, PAT INR 20 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 291 crore, up 37% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 31 crore (up 68% YoY) and margin of 10.49%, up 191 bps. PAT was INR 20 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier. Management attributed margin expansion to a mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, whose combined share rose from about 46% to 63%. Net working capital days fell to 56 from 66 at March 2026 (about 97 in the prior quarter per an analyst exchange), and management reiterated 35-40% annual growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5 crore in Q1 FY26
Guided to INR 75-80 crore by FY27 end

segments.name: B2B supply
segments.commentary: Entry point to the network; contributed about 37% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers almost all construction materials.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 84% YoY and contributed about 53% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers stone aggregates, ready-mix concrete and asphalt; about 8.65 lakh MT delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 28 crore, roughly 10% of top line, in Q1. New INR 650 crore mandate from Wadhwa Group (Mumbai); GDV under execution rose to over INR 1,800 crore from INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26. Management cited 60-65% EBITDA margin for DaaS.

segments.name: Asphalt (within contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR 53 crore from INR 30 crore in Q4 FY26; customers transacted rose to 38 from 28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.5% EBITDA margin the new baseline, and is 10.5-11% the expected range?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain is mainly mix: contract manufacturing and DaaS, which carry higher margins than B2B, rose from about 46% to 63% of revenue; management expects this to sustain for the next few quarters. Directionally, 11% next year was agreed as fair.

qa_highlights.question: How much utilisation headroom is left in contract manufacturing and how will capacity grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 65-70% on about 9 million tonnes; 2-3 million tonnes to be added in the next two quarters by recycling existing deposits, taking capacity to about 11 million tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 35-40% guidance be raised, given Q1 and Q2 are seasonally lean?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is sticking to 35-40% annual growth; first six months about 40% of sales and second half about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the credit losses and loss given default?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ECL about INR 22 crore on about INR 3,800-4,000 crore lifetime revenue. Recoveries after legal process range from 25% to over 80%, and most new receivables are insured.

qa_highlights.question: How does supply chain financing work and does it cost interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Financiers pay vendors on day one and the company gets about 90 days to pay; interest is sometimes borne by vendors and is negotiated. Management said it accepts the interest cost to reduce working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Does DaaS expose the company to real estate risk and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a RERA promoter and does not lend or commit capital; income is a fixed monthly fee, a percentage of construction and a percentage of sales, with financial closure and bank loans in place on day one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt path and what drives the rise to INR 75-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Current net debt INR 14.5 crore, net debt-to-equity 0.02x; the rise is to fund working capital for 35-40% growth, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be stronger on cash flows. Long-term net debt-to-equity to stay at 0.5-0.6x.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the customer base and what is the DaaS sales commission benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers are 45-50% of revenue, spread across projects and regions. Management cited sales-only channels charging 2-3% and some 4-5% of GDV, arguing DaaS covers far more than sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asphalt outlook and when is the subsidiary merger completed?
qa_highlights.answer: Asphalt is about six months old, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be meaningfully higher; management expects a meaningful FY27 contribution without giving numbers. Subsidiary merger: three of four regulators have cleared it and it is at the last stage, timeline not committed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35-40% annually; management said it is sticking to the same guidance rather than raising it.
Seasonality: first six months about 40% of annual sales and second half about 60%; Q3 and Q4 expected to be meaningfully better on cash flows and revenue.
Contract manufacturing contribution targeted at 55-60% of revenue; management said 55% by year-end and 60% next year was a fair understanding.
DaaS revenue expected at 9-11% of top line, growing in line with the company at 35-40%.
Net debt guided to rise to INR 75-80 crore by FY27 end from INR 14.5 crore currently; long-term net debt-to-equity to be kept at 0.5-0.6x, not more.

Directionally, EBITDA margin expected to sustain and rise with higher contract manufacturing and DaaS mix; management did not give a hard margin number. Steady-state net working capital cycle seen at 60-70 days.
capex_capacity: Contract manufacturing capacity about 9 million tonnes annually; utilisation about 65-70% as of Q1 FY27.

Plan to add 2-3 million tonnes of annual capacity in the next two quarters by recycling existing multi-year capacity deposits (about 9 million tonnes locked in), not by paying new deposits; capacity to reach about 11 million tonnes.
Capacity addition to be in South Tamil Nadu, predominantly coarse aggregates (group category stone aggregates).
Current capacity carries about INR 900 crore of inventory, per management.
Asphalt business about six months old; Q3 and Q4 expected to be meaningfully higher than the monsoon-hit Q1 and Q2.
Subsidiary merger (to remove minority interest) pending with regulators; three of four regulators have cleared it, management gave no timeline.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 revenue INR 291 crore, up 37% YoY; contract manufacturing revenue up 84% YoY and about 53% of revenue.
Contract manufacturing delivered about 8.65 lakh MT in Q1 FY27.
Asphalt revenue INR 53 crore vs INR 30 crore in Q4 FY26; customers transacted 38 vs 28.
DaaS contributed about INR 28 crore (about 10% of revenue) in Q1; new INR 650 crore Wadhwa Group mandate; GDV under execution over INR 1,800 crore vs INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26; 10 active projects.
Repeat orders 82% vs 78% in Q4 FY26; over 3,400 customers, 2,200-plus vendors, 23 states and UTs.
Top 10 customers about 45-50% of revenue, active across multiple projects; top customer active at 15-plus project sites.
Receivables grew about 15% YoY versus revenue growth of 37%; net working capital days 56 vs 66 at March 2026 and about 97 in the prior quarter per management.
Cumulative ECL provision about INR 22 crore on lifetime revenue of about INR 3,800-4,000 crore (just over 0.5%); FY26 collections above INR 1,100 crore.
risks_watch: Receivable quality and credit losses: ECL provisions and realised recoveries after default (25% to over 80%) are the key tail risk; management says most new receivables are insured.
Rising net debt from INR 14.5 crore toward INR 75-80 crore by FY27 end as working capital builds; net working capital days guided at 60-70 steady state versus 56 in Q1.
Supply chain financing dependence: interest cost borne by the company or vendors varies and is being renegotiated; a financing pull-back would affect working capital.
Competition in asphalt, which an analyst flagged as a risk to disclose; management said it is learning from the feedback.
Geographic concentration in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; expansion to other states is not a stated strategy yet.
Pace of capacity addition (2-3 million tonnes via recycled deposits) and the Q1 and Q2 seasonal slowdown; the subsidiary merger timeline remains open.
key_quotes: It's primarily a mix of increased revenue from our contract manufacturing and DaaS segment, and they are carrying meaningfully higher margins than B2B trade.
We would like to keep our net debt-to-equity at par of 0.5 to 0.6, not more than that.
Receivables grew at less than half the pace of revenue, and that discipline held even as we grew every single quarter over the past year.
We put cash flow at , it is our topmost priority.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margin and working capital trends, with figures given readily, but evasive on specifics: DaaS revenue as a percentage of GDV, subsidiary merger timing and a precise margin number were deferred to offline discussion or left undated.
